name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.145.0 — The test-case scanner no longer misreads a regex literal as division after an operator or an expression keyword. `lib/scan-test-calls.js` now opens a regex context after `+ - * % < > ~ ^` and after `typeof case await throw else in of` (alongside the existing punctuation, `return` and the `=>` arrow), while a postfix `++`/`--`, a `]`, a grouping paren and a call paren still read the next `/` as division. Before this, a regex holding a quote in one of those positions opened a string span that ran to end of file, swallowing every later line-start test()/it() call and pushing the preceding call's end to src.length. The count was merely wrong; the span is not — specs/20260911/03 deletes expired tests by that span, so an end at EOF would corrupt the file. Eight failing shapes and four division controls are pinned behaviourally, and the live repo's count is unchanged across all of its test files. 7.144.0 — Spec-number collisions are now a deterministic /spec:doctor check: spec-number-check.js refuses two live (non-superseded) specs sharing one NN- number inside a specs/YYYYMMDD/ directory, because the number is the AC-ID namespace and a duplicate lets either spec pass its review coverage leg on the other's tests. Landed with the live collision fixed — specs/20260911/04-the-client-loop.md renumbered to 06-, its eighteen AC-ids, its dependant's backlink and its plan ledger row moved with it. 7.143.0 — A repo's test count is now instrumented, not capped. `lib/scan-test-calls.js` is the one definition of a test case — a `test(`/`it(` call at line start across the host's test-classified files, blind to strings, comments and regex literals — and `count-tests.js` reports it (`tests: <count> cases`, `--json` → `{"count":N}`, never a non-zero exit for the count itself). The review's new `tests` leg records that count on every evidence manifest and is deliberately absent from every blocking set (`BLOCKING`, `REVIEW_BLOCKING`, `BLOCKING_LEGS`), so the number lands on each ledger row and can never redden a verdict. There is no limit, no ceiling file and no hook: `spec/test-ceiling.json` is deleted, and a count that could fail a build would make deleting tests the model's cheapest route to green.
